/new-patients.description: What your first visit at Riverbend Dental involves, how long it takes, what to bring and how to fill out forms online.
/new-patients.main:
Your first visit

We are accepting new patients and can usually see you within a week.

What happens

Plan on about 75 minutes. Dr. Patel will talk with you first, then take digital x-rays and photos, check your gums and every tooth, and go through what she sees on the screen with you. If you are due, the hygienist will clean your teeth the same day.

Before you arrive

Complete your forms online in about ten minutes: Fill out new-patient forms online. Bring your photo ID, your insurance card if you have one, and a list of current medications.

Cost

Exam, x-rays and cleaning are $189 without insurance. We will check your benefits before you arrive and tell you your estimated share.

Book your first visit or call (555) 030-0789.

/insurance-and-payment.title: Insurance and payment | Riverbend Dental
/insurance-and-payment.description: Plans we are in network with, how out-of-network billing works, CareCredit financing and our in-house membership plan.
/insurance-and-payment.main:
Insurance and payment, in plain English

In network

We are a participating provider (in network) with Delta Dental PPO, Cigna DPPO and MetLife PDP. We also accept Aetna and Guardian plans out of network; we file the claim for you and you pay the difference.

No insurance?

Our Riverbend Membership Plan is $29 a month: two cleanings, exams and x-rays a year, plus 15% off other treatment. There is no deductible and no waiting period.

Paying over time

We offer CareCredit financing with 0% for 12 months on treatment over $300, subject to approval.

What things cost

New-patient exam, x-rays and cleaning: $189. A single crown is typically $1,100–$1,400 before insurance. We give you a written estimate before any treatment.

Questions? Call (555) 030-0789; Maria handles benefits and will call your plan for you.

/emergency-dentist.title: Emergency dentist in Milford, OH | Riverbend Dental
/emergency-dentist.description: Tooth pain, a broken tooth or a knocked-out tooth: what to do now and how to reach Dr. Patel after hours.
/emergency-dentist.main:
Dental emergency? Here is what to do

During office hours: call (555) 030-0789. We keep two slots open each day for emergencies and will usually see you the same day.

After hours and weekends: call the same number; our answering service pages the on-call dentist, who calls you back within 30 minutes.

Is it an emergency?

  • Knocked-out adult tooth: keep it moist in milk and call now; the first hour matters.
  • Swelling of the face or jaw, fever, or trouble swallowing: go to the emergency room first, then call us.
  • Broken tooth or lost crown without severe pain: call in the morning; cover sharp edges with wax.
  • Toothache: ibuprofen as directed and call; do not put aspirin on the gum.

You do not need to be an existing patient. Bring your ID and insurance card if you have one.

/meet-dr-patel.title: Meet Dr. Anita Patel, DDS | Riverbend Dental
/meet-dr-patel.description: Dr. Anita Patel, DDS has practised in Milford since 2012. Ohio State College of Dentistry graduate, ADA and AGD member.
/meet-dr-patel.main:
Dr. Anita Patel, DDS

Dr. Patel graduated from The Ohio State University College of Dentistry in 2010 and has practised in Milford since 2012. She is a member of the American Dental Association, the Ohio Dental Association and the Academy of General Dentistry, and completes about 60 hours of continuing education a year, mostly in implant dentistry.

If you are nervous about the dentist, say so when you book. Dr. Patel will go through everything on the screen first, use nitrous oxide if you would like it, and stop whenever you raise a hand.

Outside the office she coaches her daughter's soccer team and is slowly restoring a 1972 canoe.

Book with Dr. Patel or call (555) 030-0789.

/services/dental-implants.title: Dental implants in Milford, OH | Riverbend Dental
/services/dental-implants.description: What a dental implant visit involves at Riverbend Dental, how long it takes, and what it costs before insurance.
/services/dental-implants.main:
Dental implants

An implant replaces the root of a missing tooth with a small titanium post, and a crown on top replaces the tooth. Dr. Patel places and restores implants here in Milford; she refers out when a case needs a specialist.

What the visits look like

First a 3D scan and a conversation about options, including a bridge or a partial denture if an implant is not the right fit. Placement takes about an hour under local anesthetic, with nitrous oxide if you want it. The implant heals for three to four months, then the crown is made.

Cost

A single implant with crown is typically $3,800–$4,500 before insurance. Most dental plans cover part of the crown. CareCredit financing is available.

Book an implant consultation or call (555) 030-0789.

Aftercare

Expect mild soreness for two or three days; most people are back at work the next morning. You brush and floss an implant like a natural tooth, and we check it at each cleaning. With normal care an implant should last decades.

/services/invisalign.title: Invisalign in Milford, OH | Riverbend Dental
/services/invisalign.description: Invisalign clear aligners for adults and teens at Riverbend Dental: how it works, how long, what it costs.
/services/invisalign.main:
Invisalign clear aligners

Clear aligners straighten teeth with a series of removable trays you change every week or two. Most adult cases at Riverbend take 9 to 15 months. Dr. Patel is an Invisalign provider and will tell you plainly if your case needs an orthodontist instead.

What to expect

A scan at your first visit, a preview of your result, then trays every six weeks. You wear them 22 hours a day and take them out to eat.

Cost

Comprehensive Invisalign is $4,200–$5,500 at our office; many plans with orthodontic benefits cover part of it.

Book an Invisalign consultation or call (555) 030-0789.

Is Invisalign right for you?

Aligners work well for crowding, gaps and mild bite problems. They are not the best choice for every case, and we will say so. Teens need to be disciplined about wearing them; parents get a weekly compliance check through the app. Retainers at the end are included, because teeth drift back without them.
